correctness.rationale: The language of the length-n cover is characterized by forbidden \(10^{r-1}1\) with non-power \(r<n\), yielding the exact allowed-return set and an irreducible \(n\)-state graph. Its generating function has a unique entropy root. At the original root, the missing powers have first omitted return \(Q\) and remaining tail \(O(\lambda^{-2n})\), and logarithmic derivatives differ by \(O_b(n\lambda^{-n})\); the simple-root Taylor bound proves the claimed uniform normalized error. The discrete \(t=Q-n\) dichotomy proves the complete cluster set. At non-power \(n\), the \(n\)-periodic return word witnesses strict inclusion, and mixing-SFT strict entropy monotonicity gives the plateau criterion. A complete 96-case checker run and separate high-precision boundary tests corroborate but are not used as infinite proofs. All limits require fixed \(b\).

value.rationale: Canonical SFT covers are natural finite-memory approximations and entropy-stability objects. This exact all-bases-and-cutoffs theorem quantifies their error at the true exponential scale and discovers a countably infinite, one-accumulation-point phase spectrum rather than simple convergence or an interval; the sparse exact plateau indices explain the discrete-scale effect. It is not a textbook bare renewal equation or arbitrary numerical instance, and the precise finite-resolution accuracy is relevant to computing entropy from symbolic languages.
